#### 1. Lessel-Kreienkamp syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.489)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-203927, Reactome:R-HSA-426486)

**Proposed mechanism:** PRKRA (HGNC:9373) —DISRUPTS→ RNA interference pathway (GO:0006401); AGO2 (HGNC:545) —DISRUPTS→ RNA interference pathway (GO:0006401); RNA interference pathway (GO:0006401) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); RNA interference pathway (GO:0006401) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263); RNA interference pathway (GO:0006401) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); RNA interference pathway (GO:0006401) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252). Loss-of-function mutations in PRKRA (associated with MONDO:0012789) and AGO2 (associated with Lessel-Kreienkamp syndrome) both impair the function of the RNA interference pathway. Dysregulation of this pathway, which is crucial for gene silencing and post-transcriptional regulation, can lead to a spectrum of neurodevelopmental and neurological phenotypes observed in both diseases, including intellectual disability, global developmental delay, seizures, and hypotonia.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a substantial burden of loss-of-function variants in PRKRA and AGO2 in unaffected individuals in large population databases like gnomAD would weaken this hypothesis. Conversely, demonstrating that specific variants in PRKRA and AGO2 lead to distinct and non-overlapping molecular disruptions within the RNAi pathway, without a shared downstream effect, would also falsify this proposed overlap. _(variant: Any common (AF > 0.01) loss-of-function variant in PRKRA or AGO2.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the RNAi machinery in these disorders could pave the way for therapeutic strategies that target common downstream effectors or attempt to restore RNAi function, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
